jurisdiction.reason: A result is a result in every state and for every office. The sentence and the rows inside it are generated per contest; the treatment around them is the same wherever the seat is.

missing: The end of a campaign is an unstyled bulleted list. Walked on 2026-09-22 in eleven towns across five states — Chicago, Galena, Lexington, Paducah, Reno, Ely, Kansas City, Hannibal, Baltimore, Cumberland and Sitka — and in every one of them the result reads as four lines of ordinary body text, indistinguishable from a note about groceries.
notes: Deliberately generic. One treatment serves every state, every office and every result: nothing in it may be specific to a jurisdiction, a party or an outcome.

The number of rows is NOT fixed. It was two everywhere until 2026-09-22, when the single hardcoded opponent was replaced with a field of two to four, so the artwork must hold three to five rows and cannot assume a head-to-head.
A losing result uses the same treatment as a winning one. The game's own line is that a lost election leaves the life running, so the artwork must not read as a trophy or as a defeat.
No party marks. The parties in this game are real organizations and their emblems are not ours to draw.
title: A treatment for the night a player finds out whether they won
whyNeeded: Winning or losing an election is the single largest thing that happens to a character in this game, and it is the payoff for every week the player spent on the campaign. It currently arrives with no more visual weight than a line about a meeting. A refusal to put a character on a ballot already has a request filed for it (ui-no-candidacy-refusal-panel) on exactly this reasoning; the result at the other end of the same campaign has nothing. Measured rather than assumed: eleven candidacies played to a decided result on 2026-09-22 and every one of them ended on the same four plain lines.
